name: plan-runner
description: Take a Markdown implementation plan, run it through a parallel agent swarm with per-wave verification, and generate a bug-fix plan for re-runs; TDD red-green mode on by default (--no-tdd to disable) with per-task red/green gate evidence; auto-detects Claude Code Agent Teams for token-lean orchestration with a subagent fallback. Tallies best-effort token usage for every dispatched subagent (analyzer, dev agents, verifiers, aggregator) into manifest.json token_usage with a grand total and honest coverage counters, surfaced in dashboards, an end-of-run per-phase Token Report with top consumers, and the PR stats; when the harness surfaces no usage figure for a subagent, each agent's own token_usage self-report (the last in-band harness figure, never an estimate) is used as a labeled lower-bound fallback. Agent returns are file-backed: every dev agent and verifier writes its final JSON to a durable per-agent return file the orchestrator reads as the source of truth (messages are a convenience preview), so an idle-race or teardown can no longer lose a completed verdict. On the teams backend each wave is verifier-gated: the lead waits on the verifier's file-backed verdict (never self-verifies) and a coverage gate before aggregation backfills any missing verdict, so a PR cannot open while a verifier is still outstanding; a verdict that lands after its wave was already recorded UNVERIFIABLE or superseded is reconciled by union of findings into any already-produced aggregation, fix-plan, and PR artifacts, so a slow verifier's real BUGS_FOUND can never be erased by a later CLEAN or lost to an expired bounded wait. git is optional: when absent (no binary or not a repo) all git operations are skipped. Before opening the PR, syncs a code-atlas architecture index (runs /code-atlas:update when .code-atlas/ is present) so the index reflects what was implemented. Verification coverage is configurable via a .plan-runner.yml verify_mode (per-agent | per-wave | last-wave-only) or a --verify flag; lower modes verify fewer waves, record the rest as SKIPPED (distinct from UNVERIFIABLE), and force a draft PR with a banner. Wave plans are mechanically validated before dispatch: every impl agent's tests_to_satisfy path must exist or be authored by an earlier-wave test-author, and a test-author's owned_files must be disjoint from its paired impl's (an explicit inline_tests: true opts a single-file bin-style target out), so an invented test path or a vacuous red can no longer silently pass a gate or drop a task. The green gate parses the runner's executed-test count and records a zero-test run as INVALID with valid_green: false -- never PASSED -- with an unparseable count recorded as the honest valid_green: null for the verifier to judge, mirroring the invalid-red rule. Verification is pipelined off the critical path: each wave commits first, then its verifier runs against a snapshot worktree of that commit while the next wave's dev agents work, with every verdict drained before aggregation (--sync-verify or verification.pipelined: false for the synchronous behavior); TDD gates run the full suite once per wave instead of once per agent. Large plans are sliced into sequential phases (default 4 waves each) that each execute with a fresh context -- relay mode dispatches a phase runner per phase, stop mode fully resets the host process at each boundary -- and a run-state.json checkpoint written after every wave lets an interrupted run resume from its last completed wave (--resume, --phase-size, --phase-mode, --no-phasing). Output location is auto-detected: cycle artifacts land under <docs_base>/plan-runner/, where docs_base comes from an explicit documentation-directory statement in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, else a top-level scan for docs, doc, documentation or .docs, else the docs default; the resolved base is printed at run start, recorded in the manifest, and resume discovery also scans the legacy docs/plan-runner/ path. Final step opens or updates a proper PR via the plan-runner:pr skill (conventional title, rich body, draft when bugs remain); the pr skill is an internal pipeline step, invocable only by the model (user-invocable: false) and hidden from the user slash-command menu.
